form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Markey (for himself and Ms. Warren) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

form.official-title: To establish an intercity passenger rail service investment grant program.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Building Rail Across Intercity Networks To Ride Around Interior of the Nation Act or the BRAIN TRAIN Act.

section.header: Establishment of grant program for high-performance intercity passenger rail service

subsection.text: Chapter 261 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Intercity passenger rail service investment program

paragraph.text: The term applicant means Amtrak or a State, group of States, interstate compact, or public agency established by 1 or more States with responsibility for providing intercity passenger rail service.
The term capital project means a project or program in a State rail plan developed under chapter 227 for—

subparagraph.text: acquiring, constructing, improving, or inspecting equipment, track, and track structures, or a facility of use in or for the primary benefit of intercity passenger rail service;

expenses incidental to the acquisition or construction (including designing, engineering, location surveying, mapping, environmental studies, and acquiring active or out of service rights-of-way); and

payments for the capital portions of rail trackage rights agreements, highway-rail grade crossing improvements related to intercity passenger rail service, mitigating environmental impacts, communication and signalization improvements, relocation assistance, acquiring replacement housing sites, and acquiring, constructing, relocating, and rehabilitating replacement housing.

paragraph.text: The term high-performance rail means intercity passenger rail service that is designed to meet the current and future market demand for the transportation of people, in terms of capacity, travel times, reliability, and efficiency.
The term intercity passenger rail service has the meaning given the term intercity rail passenger transportation in section 24102.
The term Secretary means the Secretary of Transportation.
The term State means any of the 50 States or the District of Columbia.
The Secretary shall establish an intercity passenger rail service investment program to promote high-performance rail transportation options.

The Secretary may award grants under this section to an applicant to finance capital projects for high-performance rail, including grants awarded in installments for projects lasting longer than 1 year.

subsection.text: Each applicant seeking a grant under this section shall submit an application to the Secretary in such form and containing such information as the Secretary shall reasonably require.

subsection.header: Competitive grant selection and criteria for grants

subparagraph.text: establish criteria for selecting among capital projects that meet the criteria specified in paragraph (2);
conduct a national solicitation for applications; and
award grants on a competitive basis.

paragraph.text: In selecting the recipients of intercity passenger rail grants under subsection (b)(2), the Secretary shall—

clause.text: the project to be part of a State rail plan developed under chapter 227, or under the plan required under section 211 of the Passenger Rail Investment and Improvement Act of 2008 (49 U.S.C. 24902 note);

the applicant or recipient to have the legal, financial, and technical capacity to carry out the project, satisfactory continuing control over the use of the equipment or facilities, and the capability and willingness to maintain the equipment or facilities;
the project to be based on the results of preliminary engineering studies or other planning;
the applicant to provide sufficient information upon which the Secretary can make the findings required under this subsection;

if an applicant has selected the proposed operator of its service, the applicant to provide written justification to the Secretary showing why the proposed operator is the best, taking into account costs and other factors;
each proposed project to meet all safety and security requirements that are applicable to the project under law; and
each project to be compatible with, and operated in conformance with—

subclause.text: plans developed pursuant to the requirements under section 135 of title 23; and
the national rail plan (if available);

clause.text: that are anticipated to result in significant improvements to intercity rail passenger service, including consideration of the project’s—

subclause.text: levels of estimated ridership, increased on-time performance, reduced trip time, or additional service frequency to meet anticipated or existing demand;
anticipated provision of intercity passenger rail service in historically and persistently unconnected and under-connected regions; and
anticipated favorable impact on air or highway traffic congestion, capacity, or safety;

clause.text: for which there is a high degree of confidence that the proposed project is feasible and will result in the anticipated benefits, as indicated by—

subclause.text: the project’s precommencement compliance with environmental protection requirements;
the readiness of the project to be commenced; and
other relevant factors determined by the Secretary; and

clause.text: for which the level of the anticipated benefits compares favorably to the amount of Federal funding requested under this section; and

subparagraph.text: give greater consideration to projects that—

clause.text: are anticipated to result in benefits to other modes of transportation and to the public at large, including consideration of the project’s—

subclause.text: encouragement of intermodal connectivity through provision of direct connections between train and transit stations, airports, bus terminals, subway stations, ferry ports, and other modes of transportation;
anticipated improvement of conventional intercity passenger, freight, or commuter rail operations;
use of positive train control technologies;
environmental benefits, including projects that involve the purchase of environmentally sensitive, fuel-efficient or electrified, and cost-effective passenger rail equipment;
anticipated reduction of greenhouse gas emissions;
anticipated improvement of air quality and public health;
anticipated positive economic and employment impacts, including development in the areas near passenger stations, historic districts, or other opportunity zones;
encouragement of State and private contributions toward station development, energy and environmental efficiency, and economic benefits; and
provision of enhanced access for persons with disabilities to intercity passenger rail service; and

clause.text: incorporate equitable financial participation in the project’s financing, including consideration of—

subclause.text: donated or discounted interests in real or personal property;
donated services;
financial contributions by intercity passenger, freight, and commuter rail carriers commensurate with the benefit expected to their operations;
financial commitments from host railroads, non-Federal governmental entities, nongovernmental entities, and others; and
Federal loans, including loans under title V of the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1976 (45 U.S.C. 821 et seq.).

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall require each recipient of a grant under this chapter to comply with the grant requirements under section 22905.

State rail plans completed before the date of enactment of the Passenger Rail Investment and Improvement Act of 2008 (division B of Public Law 110–432) that substantially meet the requirements of chapter 227 of this title, as determined by the Secretary pursuant to section 22706, shall be deemed by the Secretary to have met the requirements of paragraph (2)(A)(i).
The Federal share of the cost of a capital project financed under this section shall not exceed 90 percent of the project’s net capital cost.
The fair market value of in-kind contributions to a capital project financed under this section shall be treated as non-Federal matching funds for purposes of paragraph (1).
The value of any Federal loans paid back with non-Federal funds shall be treated as non-Federal matching funds for purposes of paragraph (1).

subsection.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary shall issue regulations to carry out this section.

paragraph.text: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $5,000,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2022 through 2026.
Any amounts appropriated for a fiscal year pursuant to paragraph (1) that remain unobligated at the end of such fiscal year shall be made available for eligible projects in the following fiscal year.

subsection.text: The chapter analysis for chapter 261 of title 49, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

toc.toc-entry: 26107. Intercity passenger rail service investment program.
